corrections.finding: A curve count is wrong and reversed. The paper averages 95 curves of 21 half particles and 120 curves of 13 reclining particles; the item says "from 21 and 120 indentation curves", which puts the particle count 21 where the curve count 95 stands and, in its own order, hands 21 to the reclining particles and 120 to the half particles, both reversed. The same clause attaches those counts to the stiffness, which the paper takes instead from the first curve at each particle. The indentation at which the shell ruptures, 3.9 ± 1.5 nm at reclining particles and 4 ± 2 nm at half particles, is dropped from the table the item otherwise quotes, and the approximately 75 pN maximal imaging force the mean heights are taken at is dropped. The opening carries a full returning to every particle where the paper has a full return at one half particle and partial returns at one reclining particle. Every other figure stands: 0.05 N/m, 38 ± 2 and 35.5 ± 2 nm, 40 and 33.5 nm by X-ray each at its own orientation, approximately 3 min, 36 to 15 nm, 15 nm as a cap, approximately 60% and approximately 10% each at its own orientation, frames 4, 7 and 10, frames 1 and 7, 0.03 ± 0.01 and 0.06 ± 0.03 N/m, 122 ± 83 and 165 ± 38 pN, 13 and 21 particles, 37 frames, 65 pN.

fixed.section: 3.7 Structural-protein surface — a matrix as a living set: a self
fixed.text: Individual vault particles lower their height under an imaging force. One half particle returns its original height when that force lowers, and one reclining particle returns part of its height. The particles are rat major vault protein expressed in HighFive insect cells from a recombinant baculovirus, sucrose-gradient purified, adsorbed on a highly ordered pyrolytic graphite surface in TMS buffer and imaged in liquid by atomic force microscopy in jumping mode, with rectangular silicon-nitride cantilevers of nominal spring constant 0.05 N/m calibrated by Sader's method. At a maximal imaging force of approximately 75 pN mean heights are 38 ± 2 nm for particles reclining on the barrel and 35.5 ± 2 nm for half particles adsorbed through the waist with the cap facing up, against 40 nm for reclining particles and 33.5 nm for half particles from X-ray. Across sequential topographies at approximately 3 min intervals with the imaging force altered frame to frame, one half particle's height drops abruptly from 36 nm to 15 nm as that force rises and returns to its original height at lower imaging force, and 15 nm matches the size of a cap alone. The strain is approximately 60% at half particles and approximately 10% at reclining particles, and the half-particle result repeats at further particles. One reclining particle loses height across the frames with partial returns at frames 4, 7 and 10, and a comparison of frames 1 and 7 carries partial collapse at the barrel. Stiffness is 0.03 ± 0.01 N/m at 13 reclining particles and 0.06 ± 0.03 N/m at 21 half particles, each the slope of the first curve at each particle. Breaking force and the indentation at which the shell ruptures are 122 ± 83 pN and 3.9 ± 1.5 nm at the 13 reclining particles, averaged across 120 indentation curves, and 165 ± 38 pN and 4 ± 2 nm at the 21 half particles, averaged across 95 indentation curves. A half particle imaged across 37 frames at a held 65 pN breaks first at the barrel, the cap tilting and the particle losing its axial symmetry.

corrections.finding: A field's explaining passes as an observing and numbers go with it. The bonding energy between two alpha-helices approximately four times that between two beta-sheet domains is the account's own estimate, from contacts of two consecutive major vault proteins determined by a program and from tabulated energies taken from elsewhere, and the three tabulated values −1.5, −4.5 and −40 kcal/mol are dropped; the 2 kBT and 8 kBT are likewise tabulated and not read here; the approximately 20 kBT is the account's own estimate from the step's distance and force; and the contact counts come from the X-ray structure and prior structural accounts, not from this microscopy. The reclining count 97 of 357 is dropped, and that count divides to 27% against the 22% the account says, two sayings parting, both kept. The single steps are at reclining particles, whose curves carry several peaks, and the orientation is dropped. The repeated-indentation observing, a drop at every curve with the structure unaltered after the cyclic loading, is lost, and it is the closest observing to a closing that goes on cycling. "fractures were detected" clocks where the item otherwise stands in the present. Every other figure stands: 650 ms, 2 s, 617 curves, 26 half and 28 reclining particles, 179 of 260, 22 events, 11 particles, 90 s, 220 ± 34 and 302 ± 34 kBT each at its own orientation, 1.3 ± 0.95 nm, 117 ± 50 pN, 29 of 41, 16, 5 and 10.

fixed.section: 3.7 Structural-protein surface — a matrix as a living set: a self
fixed.text: Fractures induced at the barrel of individual vault particles by an atomic force microscope tip close again over time while the particle stands in a liquid environment at room temperature, and the fractures run along the contacts between two neighbouring major vault proteins, in the direction those proteins align. Recovery times part into three: a restoration of force during the backward curve, under 650 ms; no restoration of force with the next topography carrying an intact particle, 650 ms to 2 s; and the fractured topography imaged whole before its recovery, over 2 s. Across 617 force-indentation curves at 26 half particles and 28 reclining particles, 179 of 260 curves at half particles, 70%, recover under 650 ms, against 97 of 357 curves at reclining particles, said there as 22% and standing at 27% on the division of those two counts. Twenty-two events of reversible topographic damage stand at 11 different reclining particles, each over 2 s, the span of a single curve, registered by switching off the y-scan and enabling only the x-scan. One reclining particle returns to its first shape within 90 s, the time to take one complete image. Under repeated indentation every curve carries a drop and the particle's structure after the cyclic loading stands unaltered, the average spring constant holding across at least the first cycle of approximately five curves. The average energy supplied across a breakage-and-recovery cycle is 220 ± 34 kBT at reclining particles and 302 ± 34 kBT at half particles. Single steps at the indentation curves of reclining particles, whose curves carry several peaks where a half particle's carry one, are 1.3 ± 0.95 nm and 117 ± 50 pN, approximately 20 kBT each at the account's own estimate from that distance and that force, against 2 kBT at a hydrophobic interaction and 8 kBT at a hydrogen bond, both tabulated values the account takes from elsewhere. Fractures stand at the barrel surface only. From the X-ray structure of the whole particle and prior structural accounts, the strongest major-vault-protein contacts stand between cap-helix domains, 29 of the 41 residue pairs at that interface hydrophobic, against 16 hydrogen bonds, 5 ionic bonds and 10 hydrophobic contacts at the barrel. A bonding energy between two alpha-helices approximately four times that between two beta-sheet domains is the field's explaining, from the noncovalent contacts of two consecutive major vault proteins determined by a program together with tabulated energies of −1.5 kcal/mol at a hydrophobic interaction, −4.5 kcal/mol at a hydrogen bond and −40 kcal/mol at an ionic pair.
